chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about a man who came to a man while he was asleep. So when he came to be upon his back, he woke up due to it, so he poked him with a knife, so he killed him. So he said: 'There is neither a wergild for him, nor a retaliation'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing someone while they are asleep in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes a unique legal precedent in Shia jurisprudence where a killer is exempt from both *qisas* (retaliation) and *diyah* (blood money) when striking a sleeping victim who was unaware of the attack. Scholars interpret this exemption as stemming from the victim's lack of active defense or immediate threat perception, distinguishing it from standard homicide cases. The ruling highlights the nuanced application of justice in Shia fiqh, balancing the severity of the act with the specific circumstances of the victim's state of consciousness.
